qa.question: Should units 4 and 5 timepoint 2 keep start year 2019 against EIA's 1977 and 1978?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 gives operating years 1977 for unit 4 and 1978 for unit 5. Those are the original coal units. GEM records the conversion year, 2019, for the converted units.
qa.recommendation: Leave 2019 as it is, since GEM's convention is the conversion year. Add the conversion permit memo as the source if a reviewer wants one.
qa.note: EIA table: https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx. Conversion permit memo: https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/4454.pdf. I could not confirm the 2019 restart date in a document.

qa.question: Does a document state that Muskogee units 4 and 5 have no carbon capture?
qa.finding: No document I read mentions carbon capture at units 4 or 5. The permit memo at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/8130.pdf lists activated carbon handling for Unit 6 mercury control, which is not carbon capture.
qa.recommendation: Leave CCS attachment as no. No source was found, so the validation item stays open for a person to dismiss.
qa.note: Looked at the permit memos from 2018 and 2021 and the harvested permit file for this plant. Not found.

qa.question: What document supports Owner and Location for Muskogee Generating Station?
qa.finding: The permit memo at https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/8130.pdf names Oklahoma Gas & Electric Company as the permit holder and gives coordinates 35.76054, -95.28731. GEM's point is about 160 meters away.
qa.recommendation: Use the permit memo as the Owner and Location source. Keep GEM's values.
qa.note: The Southwest Power Pool open queue list read on 5 November 2026 (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV) shows GEN-2025-SR9 at 400 MW, owned by OG&E, with no fuel shown, at the Muskogee 345 kV substation, with commercial operation in December 2029. It is added in this batch as a new unit at this plant. GEN-2024-293 is 248 MW of gas at the same substation name, with commercial operation in May 2033. No document ties it to this plant, so it is added as its own project.
